gaps.sentence: We stopped at a cafe to ___ a chat.
gaps.explanation: have a chat is the fixed collocation for a friendly, informal conversation.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her a compliment on her new hairstyle.
gaps.explanation: pay somebody a compliment is the fixed collocation for praising someone.

gaps.sentence: The manager ___ an announcement about the changes yesterday.
gaps.explanation: make an announcement is the fixed collocation for stating something publicly.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: We are still ___ arrangements for the wedding.
gaps.explanation: make arrangements is the fixed collocation for organising plans.

gaps.sentence: Smoking can ___ serious harm to your health.
gaps.explanation: do harm to something is the fixed phrase; 'make harm' is a common learner error.
